smell_elimination.justification: Only removes the most visible dead code (fit_weighted method and its conditional branch). All enabling infrastructure remains: backend registration system, capability detection, selection logic in utils.py, and the actual backend selection call in fit_regression() are completely untouched. This is a superficial fix that addresses symptoms while leaving the disease intact.

cross_file_coordination.justification: Makes changes only to regression.py while completely ignoring the dead code infrastructure in algorithms.py (registration system), utils.py (_select_regression_backend), and _statistics.py (capability detection). The backend_name and backend_func variables are still being assigned from _select_regression_backend() but now serve absolutely no purpose. Orphaned imports and helper functions remain scattered across modules.

structural_soundness.justification: Removes one method and one conditional branch cleanly, but leaves a structurally broken execution path: fit_regression() still calls _select_regression_backend(), assigns variables that are now completely unused, and executes dead infrastructure on every call. The architectural smell (plugin system for one built-in case) remains entirely intact.

code_quality.justification: The diff itself is clean (proper removal without introducing syntax errors), but the resulting codebase is worse from a quality perspective. Now fit_regression() has variables (backend_name, backend_func) that are assigned but never used, which is itself a code smell. All the complex infrastructure remains operational but accomplishes literally nothing.

dead_code_coverage.justification: Removes only the most obvious unreachable endpoint (fit_weighted method and its conditional). Leaves all the infrastructure that makes this code dead: _weighted_ols_fit function, registration call with impossible requirements, backend selection logic, capability detection system. This is like removing the visible tip of an iceberg while leaving the massive structure underwater.

cleanup_precision.justification: Creates new problems while fixing old ones. After this change, backend_name and backend_func are assigned from _select_regression_backend() but never used - a new form of dead code. Doesn't remove the import of backend selection functions, doesn't clean up the weighted_ols registration in algorithms.py, doesn't remove the _weighted_ols_fit helper function. The precision is poor.

dead_code_infrastructure_removal.justification: Fails catastrophically on this criterion. The entire plugin architecture remains: register_regression_backend(), _regression_backends, _backend_priorities, available_backends, and get_regression_backend() in algorithms.py are untouched. _select_regression_backend() in utils.py still exists and is still called from fit_regression(). Capability detection functions in _statistics.py remain. The weighted_ols registration call still executes at import time. Only the final consumer (fit_weighted) is removed, leaving a complete dead infrastructure that now produces unused variables.

module_cohesion_and_coupling_restoration.justification: No improvement to module coupling whatsoever. regression.py still imports and calls _select_regression_backend from utils.py, which still calls functions from algorithms.py, which still uses capability checks from _statistics.py. The entire cross-module tangle introduced by the smell remains completely intact. No reversion to the simple _has_statsmodels pattern. Module boundaries remain as violated as before.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This is a minimally superficial fix that removes only the most visible symptom (the unreachable fit_weighted method) while leaving the entire dead code infrastructure completely operational. The backend registration system, capability detection, selection logic, and cross-module coupling all remain untouched, making this essentially cosmetic surgery that fails to address the architectural smell. The fix actually makes things worse by creating unused variables (backend_name, backend_func) in the execution path.
